newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Islamists in car bomb escape bid.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Islamists in car bomb escape bid.

text.p: A car bomb exploded in central Turkey on Friday in an apparent attempt to free eight Islamist suspects being carried to court in a prison vehicle, Anatolian news agency said.
It said two gendarmerie police were wounded in the attack in the central province of Kirsehir. Other gendarmes sealed off the area and prevented the suspects from escaping, the agency said.
"A bomb loaded into a car at the side of the road was set off by a remote control bomb...as the armoured prison vehicle was going past," Anatolian said.

The prisoners were being taken to Ankara where they were to appear in a state security court on charges related to the killing of 37 people, most of them members of a liberal, heterodox Moslem sect, in an Islamist arson attack in 1993.
Dozens of people have been convicted in the case but the appeals court later called for retrials and tougher sentences.
Anatolian said security forces had begun a wide-ranging operation to track down the bombers.
